title: Integral numerators for rational finite matrices on compact schemes
statement: Let ℓ be prime, E a normed extension of Q_ℓ and X a compact scheme. Put F=Ext for [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]. For any n,m and morphism f:F(O_X^n)→F(O_X^m) there exist k≥0 and g:O_X^n→O_X^m with F(g)=ℓ^k f. The module objects O_X^n are the standard finite free objects.

source.place: Section 6.8, coefficient localization and Lemma 6.8.13, first paragraph; agent intersection/matrix variant

proof.text: Transport a rational regular endomorphism through the canonical continuous coefficient realization and evaluate at the unit. Localization of continuous functions on compact X gives an integral numerator for its continuous coefficient after multiplication by ℓ^k. Construct the integral multiplication map and transport it back through the coefficient equivalence.
The coefficient compatibility square and regularExtensionIso_naturality identify scalar extension of this integral map with the required multiple of the rational map.

Extract all matrix entries using finite biproducts and apply the regular result. Take the finite supremum of their exponents, multiply each numerator by the missing power, and assemble the matrix with biproduct.matrix. Compare every entry using the biproduct comparison for F. If either rank is zero the finite supremum is zero and extensionality is vacuous.

lean.statement:
theorem integralFiniteFree_clear_denominators (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (E : Type) [NormedField E] [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[ℓ] E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] (n m : ℕ)
    (f : (Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap (integralScalarMap ℓ E) X)).obj
        (Mod.finiteFree (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X) n) ⟶
      (Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap (integralScalarMap ℓ E) X)).obj
        (Mod.finiteFree (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X) m)) :
    ∃ (k : ℕ) (g : Mod.finiteFree (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X) n ⟶
        Mod.finiteFree (condensedRingObj (integralCoeff ℓ E) X) m),
      (Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap (integralScalarMap ℓ E) X)).map g =
        ℓ ^ k • f
